feed.title: NPR Topics: World
feed.subtitle: NPR world news, international art and culture, world business and financial markets, world economy, and global trends in health, science and technology. Subscribe to the World Story of the Day podcast and RSS feed.

entry.title: For some Brazilians, this election is a vote on Trump
entry.summary: President Trump says he's been having success winning races in Latin America. As Brazilian voters go to the polls, they're also deciding how much influence Trump should have in their country.

entry.title: France arrests 5,000 people, mostly teens, as school protests spread
entry.summary: High school students say their classrooms are overcrowded, teachers are missing and buildings need repairs. The protests have spread to cities across France, and some 5,000 people have been arrested.

entry.title: U.S. withdrawal from Iraq is complete
entry.summary: Twenty-three years after President George W. Bush's campaign of "shock and awe," the U.S. military has completed its withdrawal from Iraq.

entry.title: Lula or Bolsonaro? Some Brazilian voters say they don't want either
entry.summary: Brazil's election enters its final day of campaigning as Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro make their last pitches to voters. Brazilians explain what worries them, and why some still can't choose.

entry.title: Brazil's big political rematch: What to know about the Brazilian election
entry.summary: Four years after President Lula narrowly defeated Jair Bolsonaro, Brazil is back at the ballot box. This time, Lula faces Bolsonaro's son, Flávio, in a high-stakes rematch.

entry.title: How Brazil's two leading presidential candidates are talking about crime
entry.summary: Crime is at the top of voters' concerns in Brazil ahead of Sunday's national elections. Many are calling for tougher measures — part of a broader rightward shift across Latin America.

entry.title: The G7 will release 100 million reserve barrels of diesel fuel over the next 4 months
entry.summary: After increased pressure from Washington, the G7 held an emergency meeting on energy. The world's wealthiest nations say they will release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel fuel in their reserves.

entry.title: Germany's political center fights for relevance after far-right and far-left gains
entry.summary: Centrist politicians are soul-searching after electoral gains by the far right and the far left. Today's weak coalitions, political fragmentation and dire economy echo a past that led to the rise of fascism.

entry.title: October 1 ushered in a new era in U.S. foreign aid. What's the plan? Will it work?
entry.summary: The America First strategy asks for a Memorandum of Understanding as a condition for healthcare and development aid. It's been praised for promoting self-reliance but criticized for its conditions.

entry.title: Cloaked in anonymity, Israeli soldiers describe mass civilian killings in 'NAZA'
entry.summary: NAZA is an acronym for nezek agavi, Hebrew for "collateral damage." It refers to the number of civilian casualties the Israeli military deems acceptable. The documentary is made by Israeli filmmakers.
